versions.author: worker
versions.content:
# ACCT-200 Journal entries and reconciliations

1. Every manual journal entry has a preparer and a different approver. No one approves an entry they prepared,
   even if the system routes it to them. Approvers: staff entries, the senior accountant up to $50,000 and the
   assistant controller or controller above; the senior accountant's own entries, the assistant controller or
   controller.
2. Balance sheet accounts are reconciled monthly to independent support (bank statement, subledger, schedule) by
   WD3 and reviewed by WD4. Every reconciling item is identified, explained and dated.
3. Unexplained differences are never written off or posted to suspense without the controller's written
   approval.
4. Accruals: expenses incurred in the month are accrued when the invoice hasn't arrived (receiving records,
   shipping logs, contracts). Payroll: policy 3.2.
5. Prepaids are amortized straight-line over the service period; anything whose period has ended is expensed.

versions.author: worker
versions.content:
# Policy 3.2: month-end payroll accrual

Accrue wages for the open biweekly period: estimated gross wages for the period (use the last completed
period's gross from ADP) x (working days of the period that fall in the month / 10), plus employer FICA at
7.65%. Benefits are booked monthly from invoices and are not part of this accrual. Reverse on the first day of
the next month.

versions.author: worker
versions.content:
# ACCT-410 Capitalization

Capitalize individual items costing $5,000 or more with a useful life over one year (asset accounts 1500-1590),
including freight, installation and non-refundable taxes. Items under $5,000 are expensed, even if bought
together. Tooling and fixtures: 1540, 5-year life. Computer equipment: 1560, 3-year life. Depreciation starts
the month after the asset is placed in service, straight-line, no salvage.

versions.author: worker
versions.content:
# ACCT-500 Revenue recognition

- Revenue is recognized when control passes under the shipping terms: FOB Shipping Point at shipment, FOB
  Destination on delivery (proof of delivery date).
- Bill-and-hold: allowed only if all of ASC 606-10-55-83 is met: (a) a substantive reason (for example, the
  customer asked for it in writing); (b) the product is identified separately as the customer's; (c) it is ready
  for physical transfer; (d) Westerby cannot use it or send it to another customer. The controller approves every
  bill-and-hold arrangement in writing before month end.
- Month-end cutoff: Accounting reviews the shipping log for the last three days of the month and the first three
  of the next.

documents.title: TRE-600 Payments, vendor master and confidential data

versions.author: worker
versions.content:
# TRE-600 Payments, vendor master and confidential data

6.1 Vendor bank changes: AP verifies by calling the vendor at the phone number already in the vendor master
    (never a number in the request), and a second person approves the change in NetSuite. Accounting never
    changes vendor banking.
6.2 Positive pay: the bank reports exceptions by 9:00 a.m.; Accounting decides pay or return by 2:00 p.m. ET.
    Default is return.
6.3 Customer refunds: AR prepares, the controller approves, after confirming the credit is real.
7.1 Payroll registers, SSNs and bank details go to auditors only through Suralink, never by email.
7.2 Results go outside the company (sponsor, lender) only from the CFO or controller after review.
